# awscc_ec2_transit_gateway_attachment_nat_configuration (Data Source)

Data Source schema for AWS::EC2::TransitGatewayAttachmentNatConfiguration



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) Uniquely identifies the resource.

### Read-Only

- `arn` (String) Synthetic ARN encoding the NAT configuration's identity (the transit gateway attachment ID). Transit Gateway does not issue an ARN for a NAT configuration; this value exists so the configuration has a primary identifier, and it is not accepted by any EC2 API.
- `nat_gateway_rules` (Attributes Set) The complete set of NAT rules for the attachment. Updating this property replaces the entire rule set: rules omitted from the new value are removed. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--nat_gateway_rules))
- `nat_gateway_support` (String) Whether NAT gateway support is enabled on the attachment. Set to disable to stage NAT rules without activating them; the rules are retained and become active when this is later set to enable.
- `nat_system_route_support` (String) Whether routes for the NAT CIDRs are installed into the transit gateway route tables associated with the attachment. Whether this is configurable depends on the attachment; where the value is forced, supplying the opposite value is rejected. Omitting this property leaves the setting to the service: on a new configuration the service applies the attachment's default, but on an attachment where the value is configurable it keeps the value already in effect rather than reverting to that default. Removing this property from a template, or deleting this resource, therefore leaves the setting at its last value rather than restoring the default, and a resource later created on the same attachment without this property inherits that value.
- `transit_gateway_attachment_id` (String) The ID of the transit gateway attachment to configure NAT on.

<a id="nestedatt--nat_gateway_rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `nat_gateway_rules`

Read-Only:

- `match_source_cidr` (String) The source CIDR that the rule matches on.
- `nat_cidr` (String) The CIDR that the matched source addresses are translated to.
- `rule_number` (Number) The rule number.
